beginner.headline: Trump Says Musk Restored Starlink Internet in Ukraine
beginner.brief: Ukraine uses an internet system called Starlink. The military needs this fast internet to operate drones. Recently, the military had a problem with slow speeds. The slow internet made it hard to stop attacks. Donald Trump said that Elon Musk restored the access. Now, reporters say the system is working normally again.

intermediate.headline: Trump Says Musk Brought Back Ukrainian Internet Access
intermediate.brief: US President Donald Trump claims that Elon Musk has brought back internet access for Ukraine's armed forces. Trump made these comments after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said the satellite network was still limited. The recent speed limit made Ukraine's offensive equipment powerless against Russian attacks. Modern warfare often relies on high-speed internet to effectively direct unmanned vehicles. Trump refused to discuss a report that he personally called Musk to lift the restrictions. The journal reported that the system was working more normally shortly after their conversation. Ukraine relies on the service for various uses, and Elon Musk has repeatedly denied restricting access. Meanwhile, Musk has suggested that the US government ultimately controls this specific network.

advanced.headline: Trump Claims Musk Reinstated Starlink Access for Ukraine
advanced.brief: US President Donald Trump claims that Elon Musk has reactivated full access to Ukraine’s satellite internet network, following reports that deliberate limitations had severely hampered Kyiv's tactical maneuvers. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky previously noted that connectivity to the highly secure Starshield network, provided by Musk's infrastructure, had yet to be fully re-established. The connectivity limitations coincided with Trump pressuring Zelensky to halt Ukrainian aerial strikes on Russian oil refineries, which the US leader argued were causing global prices to surge. Facing crucial midterm elections next month, Trump also waived specific sanctions on Moscow and approved a controversial deal to import Russian diesel. According to unnamed officials, Trump contacted Musk to express frustration that the network's data speeds remained severely capped. These artificial speed limits rendered Ukraine's frontline interceptors practically useless against incoming Russian strikes. Although Trump refused to confirm whether he directly asked Musk to lift the limitations, he confidently asserted that the service had been successfully reinstated. For his part, Musk has consistently denied deliberately throttling the network, which is vital for targeting remote positions and protecting the country. Furthermore, the tech entrepreneur suggested that the US government might be responsible for the limitations, as the Pentagon fundamentally controls access to the secure platform. Nevertheless, the White House has categorically denied issuing any formal orders to curtail the crucial satellite service.
